clue.text: Birds bombarded with chaff or flowers ?

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or chaff them, so birds pelted with chaff have been ragged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether those birds are being pelted with husks or with blossoms.
explanation.walkthrough: The words read as 'robins ragged', which turned round names the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged robin is a pink wild plant of damp meadows, with ragged petals, so the plural names its blooms.

clue.text: Suite in VIP's train

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of attendants
second meaning: the followers trailing behind an important person

explanation.surface: A grand set of rooms booked aboard a dignitary's railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Suite and train look like a hotel room and a railway, but both mean a body of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the band of attendants who accompany a dignitary, also called a suite or train.

clue.text: Compass of notes early in the passage

indicators.note: one word sitting in another means its letters are placed inside that word

parts.note: a gut is a narrow channel or strait

explanation.surface: A musician describing the range of notes heard near the start of a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks musical, but here it is a narrow waterway, a gut.
explanation.definitionFit: The full range of musical notes, from lowest to highest, is the whole scale or range a voice can cover.

clue.text: Wrong to rouse Nero ? Awfully!

indicators.note: done awfully means botched, so the letters come out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A courtier is warned that waking the emperor Nero would be a dreadful mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistaken or incorrect can be called wrong, an adjective of the same sense.

clue.text: Author detailed to do this to his books

definitions.note: the verb a reader performs on an author's books

indicators.note: de-tailed means with its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Charles Reade, Victorian novelist of The Cloister and the Hearth

explanation.surface: An author is described at length, as if one should study him thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'described minutely', but it means losing the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: What anyone does with a novelist's books is peruse them, which is the verb here.

clue.text: They mix tea and whisky

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kitchen machines that whizz ingredients together

definitions.note: elliptical: the trade names for those who blend these
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the trade specialists who combine varieties of these drinks into a house product

explanation.surface: Someone serves an odd cocktail of tea laced with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a single odd drink, but the teas are mixed with other teas and the whiskies with other whiskies.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric mixing machines share their name with firms or experts that combine several varieties into one consistent product.

clue.text: Material used in many long dresses

indicators.note: the letters needed are put to use inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of 'many' runs into the start of 'long'; 'dresses' completes the surface

explanation.surface: A fabric that turns up in plenty of full-length gowns.
explanation.definitionFit: This synthetic fibre is woven into cloth, a fabric or material for clothing and stockings.

clue.text: Jump points and get trapped by these

definitions.note: the definition describes the things, a noun plural

parts.note: two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Leap the wrong way and you are caught in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A springe is an old word for a noose or snare used for catching small game and birds.

clue.text: Man of property, being in the French environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Latin for being, as in in esse

explanation.surface: A property owner living among French surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSE, Latin for being, is a familiar crossword word from phrases like in esse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holding a house or land on a lease has an interest in that property.

clue.text: The less wild way of the conqueror

explanation.surface: A gentler route taken by some great conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: Timur, known in English as Tamburlaine or Tamerlane, was the fourteenth-century Turco-Mongol empire builder.

clue.text: Falling away of the northern Europeans, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the words and listen to what they sound like

parts.note: the Lapps are the Sami people of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A decline among the peoples of the far north of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling off, decline or slip from a standard is a noun sense matching this word.

clue.text: Observer's Job is nothing if not hearty

indicators.note: not hearty means lacking its heart, so the middle letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written; its centre letter is the fourth of seven

explanation.surface: A cynic says a watcher's work amounts to nothing unless it is done with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking note of things, remarking and watching them, is the business of anyone who observes.

clue.text: All said and done, perhaps they impede breathing

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words could be arranged otherwise, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: When all is said and done, these may be what blocks your breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase 'all said and done' hides the fodder: only 'said' and 'done' are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen lymph tissue at the back of the nose, especially in children, can obstruct airflow.

clue.text: Newsman tried getting round difficulty

indicators.note: something in difficulty is in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a round shape, the letter O

explanation.surface: A journalist attempted to work his way around a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper's content is a journalist, a newsman in older usage.

clue.text: One who acquitted himself well as Pope ?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a man cleared of a charge, found not guilty
second meaning: the regnal name taken by thirteen popes

explanation.surface: A pontiff who performed creditably in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acquitted himself well' means performed creditably, but read literally it is a verdict of not guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A person cleared by a court is guiltless, and the same word was the regnal name of thirteen popes.

clue.text: Dismiss the members for sport

parts.note: in biology a sport is a plant or animal that differs oddly from its type, also called a rogue

explanation.surface: A club sends its members away so they can go and play games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like games, but it is the biologist's word for a freak variant.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch discontinues a session of Parliament, sending its MPs away, without dissolving it.

clue.text: Cashing in on Nigel's air-of confusion

indicators.note: an air of confusion suggests muddle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nigel looks bewildered while he profits from something.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert assets into money, selling them for their value, is a financial sense of this verb.

clue.text: Get production of soft steel up sevenfold

indicators.note: a production makes something new from raw material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for soft

explanation.surface: A steel mill is told to multiply its output of mild steel seven times.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven times as great, from Latin septem, is the multiplier this adjective expresses.

clue.text: Criminal of note in strange disorder

indicators.note: one word in another means its letters sit inside that word
disorder means confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A notorious crook found in an odd state of confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an armed gang of lawbreakers is a criminal, the noun matching here.

clue.text: Highly coloured swimmer, but not loud

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical mark for loud

explanation.surface: A brightly hued fish that makes no noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' also means gaudy, which makes it look like part of the definition, but it is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means over-bright and gaudy, so highly coloured in an unpleasantly showy way.

clue.text: Sun god's not out producing fruit

explanation.surface: The sun god stays indoors and grows crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is classed as a fruit, the kind found in cakes and puddings.

clue.text: Wedding — then Jack goes on the staff

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word that precedes Jack in the name of the British flag flown on a flagstaff

clue.text: "But, soft! what light through yonder breaks'.'" (? R and J)

clue.text: Outlet for brains ?

clue.text: Give instruction to an archer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: William, the Swiss hero who shot an apple from his son's head

clue.text: Wilderness, first rate do

A1, top class, with the digit read as the letter I

clue.text: What is stated to be foolish talk about shaking dice

clue.text: In a word no US news

definitions.note: cryptic: no and US joined into a single word
definitions.meaning: first meaning: run the two words together and you get nous, common sense
second meaning: information, as in military reports

explanation.surface: A brief report that there is no American news.

explanation.definitionFit: Nous means quick wits or brains, and the same word also means information, especially secret reports.
